packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-11 - FIRST READING FROM IMAGES ONLY (UNVERIFIED)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of
this leaf or an earlier reading of it. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001.jpg
to image-010.jpg of this packet. I did nothing beyond the rules. I make no
attempt to name work or author.

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)

- Two overviews: image-001.jpg (face A) and image-006.jpg (face B). Tiles
  image-002..005 cover face A top to bottom; image-007..010 cover face B top to
  bottom. Neighbouring tiles overlap by two or three lines.
- The object is a narrow vertical strip, about 4 cm wide by the scale bar and
  roughly 14 cm tall, upright as photographed. Edges are torn and irregular;
  there is a horizontal tear with small round holes (sewing holes?) about three
  quarters of the way down and a vertical slit near the foot.
- Single column of text as preserved, about 31-33 lines per face. The strip
  appears to be cut from a wider column: on face A the right edge cuts through
  writing on most lines; on face B the left edge is abraded and the line
  beginnings are faint or lost. I cannot tell from the crop whether the column
  was originally wider on both sides.
- Script: very small, heavily abbreviated cursive-influenced book hand in brown
  ink, with many superscript letters. Face A is rubbed, especially the middle
  third; face B is faded along its left half.
- No running title visible. No enlarged initial.
- Red: short horizontal red strokes run through or under single words at
  several points (face A: image-003 line 10, image-004 lines 4, 6, 11,
  image-005 line 5; face B: image-007 lines 4 and 11, image-008 lines 9, 10,
  13, image-009 line 5, image-010 lines 3 and 4). They mark a word that begins
  a new unit, usually just after a paraph-like flourish. A red paraph or
  red-touched letter sits at the right edge of face A (image-002 lines 1 and 4).
  A red stroke stands above the first line of face B. Red pen flourishing
  (part of a marginal ornament or of a large initial belonging to something
  to the right) runs up the lower right edge of face B (image-010).
- No interlinear or marginal gloss seen; the superscripts are abbreviation
  letters belonging to the main line.

Tentative interpretation (not observation): the repeated red-marked word looks
like "Aliqn" (Aliquando) and the surrounding wording ("ut ...", "dicitur",
"longa", "biuis"?) suggests a text that lists cases with examples, each
introduced by a red-marked catchword. I do not infer more than that.

2. SPANS SELECTED

Face A: lines 1-10 of image-002 (the clearest), the red-marked openings in
image-003/004, and the last seven lines in image-005.
Face B: the red-marked openings and the darker right half of most lines in
image-007 to image-010.
Unread or barely read: face A image-003 lines 3-9 and image-004 lines 5-10
(rubbed to traces); the left third of nearly every line on face B.

Conventions: (?) follows an uncertain reading; ( ) holds a proposed expansion;
[illegible] = ink present but not readable; [...] = lost at the cut or tear;
7 = Tironian et; 9 = the -us/con- sign; superscript letters are written ^x.
Readings below are letter-shape readings, many of them weak.

5. LIMITATIONS

- This is a weak reading. The hand is tiny and compressed, the tiles resolve
  individual strokes only on the darkest lines, and both faces are rubbed.
  Almost every word above carries a (?) and should be treated as a letter-shape
  proposal, not as established text. The firmest items are: the recurring
  red-marked word that I read "Aliqn"; "legunt" (image-007 line 4); "ut
  barbar9" (image-007 line 5); "quedam spes" (image-007 line 6); "longa"
  (image-005 line 6 and image-010 line 3); "eburne9" (image-010 line 5).
- The recurring group I print as "7 3 biuis" may be a formula of another shape
  (for example a two-letter abbreviation followed by a word ending in -iuis);
  I could not resolve it.
- Line ends on face A and line beginnings on face B are lost or faint, so no
  line is complete and no continuous sentence could be recovered.
- Which face is recto is not determinable from the images.
- A raking-light or infrared image, or a higher-magnification scan of the
  rubbed middle of face A and the left half of face B, would be needed to go
  further.
